sentences.text: Cathayornis yandica was a small bird featuring an elongated, toothy beak and feet specifically adapted for perching.
Like other Enantiornithes, a group of early birds, Cathayornis possessed large claws on its first two wing fingers that were used for support.
This species is distinguished from similar birds like Sinornis by its larger size and a shorter, straighter first finger with a longer claw.
Only one definitive fossil specimen, catalogued as IVPP V9769, is currently known for Cathayornis yandica.
Cathayornis yandica serves as the type species, meaning it is the specific species upon which the entire genus Cathayornis is based.
Cathayornis yandica was one of the first Enantiornithes species discovered in China.
The genus Cathayornis was originally described by Zhou, Jin, and Zhang in 1992.
Several species previously assigned to Cathayornis have since been reclassified or deemed invalid by later researchers.
Cathayornis is classified within the subclass Enantiornithes.
In 2002, Paul Sereno and colleagues classified Cathayornis as a junior synonym of Sinornis, a taxonomic decision that remains part of ongoing scientific discussion.
Cathayornis lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
This bird lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
Cathayornis inhabited the Early Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation in what is now Liaoning, China.
Researchers questioned the validity of Cathayornis aberransis after finding its distinguishing features, such as a skull crest, were inaccurately described.
